t.7.33.1: The sage Pulastya heard of that capture of Rāvaṇa, which was like seizing the wind itself, as it was told by the deities in heaven.
t.7.33.2: Then, shaken by affection for his son's son, the great sage of mighty steadfastness came to see the lord of Māhiṣmatī.
t.7.33.3: Taking the path of the wind, that twice-born one, moving as swift as the wind, his vigor spurred by anguish of mind, reached the city of Māhiṣmatī.
t.7.33.4: He entered the city, which resembled Amarāvatī and was thronged with joyful, well-nourished people, just as Brahmā enters Indra's Amarāvatī.
t.7.33.6: Hearing those words, "It is Pulastya," the lord of the Haihayas raised his joined palms to his head and went forth to meet that foremost of the twice-born.
t.7.33.5: Then, recognizing him as he descended, exceedingly hard to behold, like the sun come down to walk on foot, they announced him to Arjuna.
t.7.33.7: His family priest, taking the guest-offering of water and likewise the madhuparka, went forth in front of the king, as Bṛhaspati goes before Indra.
t.7.33.8: Then Arjuna, seeing that sage approaching like the rising sun and arrived before him, paid him reverence, as Indra bows to Īśvara.
t.7.33.9: Having madhuparka, water for the feet and the guest-offering presented to him, that lord of kings spoke to Pulastya in a voice choked with joy.
t.7.33.10: Today this Māhiṣmatī has been made equal to Amarāvatī, since today, O lord of the lords of the twice-born, I behold one who is rarely seen.
t.7.33.11: Today, O divine one, all is well with me; today my lineage is uplifted, since I bow to these feet of yours, which are worthy of worship by the hosts of gods.
t.7.33.12: Here is the kingdom, here are our sons, here are our wives, and here are we ourselves. O Brahman, what shall we do, what is to be done? Let your honour command us.
t.7.33.13: Having asked that king about his welfare in matters of dharma, his sacred fires and his servants, Pulastya then spoke to Arjuna, the king of the Haihayas.
t.7.33.14: O lord of kings, whose eyes are like spotless lotuses and whose face is like the full moon, incomparable is your strength, by which Daśagrīva was conquered by you.
t.7.33.15: He for fear of whom the ocean and the wind would stand motionless, this grandson of mine, exceedingly hard to conquer, has today been bound by you.
t.7.33.16: Dear son, that glory of yours is abundant, and your name has been proclaimed far and wide by you. Entreated today at my word, release Daśānana, my child.
t.7.33.17: Then Arjuna, lord of the lords of kings, accepting Pulastya's command without uttering a word, gladly released the lord of the Rākṣasas.
t.7.33.18: Having released that enemy of the gods, Arjuna honored him with divine ornaments, garlands and garments. Having entered into a friendship free of harm, sealed in the presence of fire, he bowed to the son of Brahmā and went home.
t.7.33.19: The mighty lord of the Rākṣasas, having also met with Pulastya, was shown hospitality with an embrace and was sent away, filled with shame.
t.7.33.20: And Pulastya too, son of the Grandsire and foremost among sages, having secured the release of Daśagrīva, went to the world of Brahmā.
t.7.33.22: Thus, O delight of the Rāghavas, there are always those mightier than the mighty; one who desires his own welfare should never show contempt toward another.
t.7.33.21: Thus Rāvaṇa, having suffered humiliation at the hands of Kārtavīrya, obtained his release once more through the words of Pulastya.
t.7.33.23: Then that king of the flesh-eaters, having gained the friendship of Sahasrabāhu, again wrought slaughter among men and roamed the whole earth out of pride.
